Description: e-puck should not move automatically when the project starts. It should wait for a user command.
Reduce the world size or increase the e-puck size for better visibility.
Routes should represent available paths and should not look like fixed colour-coded tracks followed by the robot.
Head gesture recognition and voice recognition should work together in the same main controller/system.
The robot should wait until the user says “Start”. After START, both voice and head gesture controls should become active.
Support S?A, A?S, S?B, B?S, A?B and B?A, including short and long/alternative routes.
“Go to A/B/S” should navigate the robot to the selected location using the shortest route from its current location.
If the user says “Turn Right/Left” during navigation, ask whether to change destination, use a different route, or continue the current route.
After a route or destination change, navigation should continue/recalculate from the robot’s current position.
STOP should have the highest priority and stop the robot immediately.
Add clear states such as IDLE, ACTIVE, NAVIGATING, PAUSED and ARRIVED/STOPPED.
Add gesture threshold, holding time and cooldown to prevent accidental or repeated commands.
Show recognised voice/head commands and current robot status in the console/UI.
Stop automatically after reaching the destination and wait for the next command.
Invalid or unclear voice commands should not cause robot movement.
Handle conflicting voice and head gesture commands using clear command-priority rules.
Clearly differentiate available routes, selected route, destination and current robot position.
Implement actual shortest-path and alternative-path selection instead of only fixed movement sequences.
Ensure routes avoid walls, benches and other obstacles in the environment.
Use e-puck sensors where possible to detect obstacles and stop safely.
Clearly define START, STOP, FORWARD, REVERSE, LEFT, RIGHT, GO TO A, GO TO B and GO TO S commands.
Allow voice/head-gesture commands while autonomous destination navigation is running.
Keep voice recognition and head-gesture recognition active together instead of switching between separate modes.
Record recognition accuracy, response time, successful execution and failed commands for project evaluation.
